extracted.intended_audience: mathematics educators, researchers in mathematics education, and scholars in philosophy of mathematics
extracted.subtask_description: A scholarly/book-chapter treatment arguing that proofs — not theorems — are the primary bearers of mathematical knowledge and examining the implications of that claim for mathematics education and the teaching of proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofs as bearers of mathematical knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Proofs rather than theorems that are the bearers of mathematical knowledge’ (central thesis quoted from Rav and examined by the authors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as the chapter's central thesis: to treat proofs themselves as the primary vehicles for mathematical knowledge rather than treating theorems in isolation. The chapter examines the consequences of adopting this view for mathematical practice and education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofs convey strategies and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofs convey important elements of mathematics such as strategies and methods (explicit claim from the abstract).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize that proofs contain not just correctness but procedural and heuristic content (strategies, methods) that are educationally valuable; teaching should therefore expose and make explicit these elements within proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primacy of proofs as the focus of mathematical interest
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim that 'proofs should be the primary focus of mathematical interest' rather than other artifacts (e.g., statements alone).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication for curriculum and pedagogy: shift emphasis from rote statement learning to engagement with proofs, their structure, and their explanatory/strategic content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance for mathematics education and teaching of proof
rubrics_metrics.description: The chapter discusses the significance of the above ideas for mathematics education in general and for the teaching of proof in particular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides educators to consider how adopting a proofs-centered perspective affects curriculum design, classroom practices, and objectives for students' proof comprehension and production; the chapter aims to articulate pedagogical implications and recommendations (full details in the chapter body beyond the abstract).
